rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a bullet that restates doctrine, comments on the training's own design, or closes with a content-free koan reads as rigour while adding nothing — wasted slide real estate and a tell the student learns to skim past. First-ever pass of this rule against this body (rule added to the compendium 2026-08-25, one day before this run). Checked all 20 body bullets against the three classes. Closest case for (a) doctrine restatement / (c) aphorism kicker: chunk 6's closing bullet (line 39) 'An un-merged branch is not unfinished work. Holding the merge until control is earned is the control working.' — its two clauses closely echo the chunk's own line 36 ('never merged... that is the shape, not an accident') and line 38 ('Control is exercised at the merge... merge waits until the work survives it'). Stays inside the rule rather than being filed: (i) this exact three-bullet unit (lines 36, 38, 39) has a dated, maintainer-authored accept-note ('Merge bullet accepted as written', 2026-08-19) that names lines 36 and 39 verbatim as the bullets that bound line 38 and states 'the beat resolves as a unit... do not add a reconciling clause' — a §16 finding here would be asking to alter a passage the maintainer has already reviewed and fixed in shape; (ii) on content, line 39's first clause pre-empts a specific, plausible misreading (that leaving work unmerged all module means it is incomplete), which is a 'tell' the rule's own earning test credits, not pure restatement; its second clause gives the withholding-action a name ('the control working') that the file uses as this chunk's takeaway, mirroring chunk 5's parallel move of naming 'Control is interrogation' as its consolidating handle. Second-closest case, chunk 1 line 7 ('A name is a handle, not a lesson... Naming it makes the move findable on Tuesday, transferable to a teammate, and checkable when it stops working.') — considered against class (b) self-referential design commentary, but it asserts a general engineering claim about the value of naming (findable, transferable, checkable), not 'you are inside a pedagogy' framing like the rule's own examples ('un-packaged first is by design'); it motivates the naming that follows without narrating the curriculum's own design choices. Chunk 7's closing bullet (line 45, 'Nothing from the near half retires...') recaps four named laws but functions as the file's designed forward-closer (per the maintainer's Slide-growth-pass note on this exact slide) and ends on a new open question ('how do you trust work you didn't watch?'), not a content-free restatement. No bullet in chunks 2, 3, 4, or 5 fits any of the three classes — each adds a distinct move, mechanism clause, or concrete example not already stated elsewhere in its chunk.
